svg.aria-label: Who owns what: a matrix of six cross-cutting rules against four columns. Three columns are the exit proofs: the Devtool checklist, now held by FIX-1481, and the DevForce proof path and the multi-seat collab scenario, both still unfiled placeholders. The fourth column is FIX-1467, the exploration that is Done and merged. Row ER-1, a non-human seat owns the task: the collab column owns it, the Devtool column consumes it, the DevForce column consumes it, FIX-1467 is blank. Row ER-2, Waiting-on-you is parked with a reason: the Devtool column owns it as FIX-1481 and is marked checklist row 4, the collab column consumes it, FIX-1467 and DevForce are blank. Row ER-3, every proof runs on a live hired Workforce: the DevForce column owns it because its path stands the workforce up, and the Devtool and collab columns consume it. Row ER-4, every proof composes and adds no layer: the Devtool column is marked builds it, and the DevForce and collab columns are marked builds if filed. Row ER-18, the downstream-blocking walls: FIX-1467's cell is marked MET, with the noun, the migration and the grant model all answered by its merge, and the Devtool column consumes it at checklist row 6. Last row, the done condition, now three separate rules: the Devtool column holds ER-Devtool marked HELD, NOT RUN, the DevForce column holds ER-DevForce marked NO CHILD, and the collab column holds ER-Collab marked NO CHILD — two empty cells on the diagonal, and the done condition owned in one part of three, with nothing yet proved. A legend distinguishes the one committed owner, a consumes cell that must not be re-decided, a conditional cell that applies once the row is filed, a MET cell, a HELD cell where a child is filed but nothing has run, and a NO CHILD cell where nothing in the set produces the rule; a blank cell means the row does not touch that rule. Notes record that kitchen-sink FIX-1455 no longer has a column because it left the set on September 20, that ER-1, ER-2 and ER-3 were re-owned rather than left pointing at it, that ER-15 was rewritten and ER-19 retired, and that nineteen further rules bind every row equally and need no column.
svg.text: WHO OWNS WHAT — ONE EXIT PROOF IS HELD, TWO HAVE NO CHILD

g.text: ER-1 · a non-human seat owns the task
ER-2 · Waiting-on-you is parked, with a reason
ER-3 · a live hired Workforce, not a mock
ER-4 · every proof composes, adds no layer
the done condition — now three rules
the one committed owner — decides or builds it
consumes it, and must not re-decide it — not a wait
conditional — applies once that row is filed
MET — satisfied, with what satisfied it recorded
NO CHILD — nothing in the set produces this
HELD — a child is filed, nothing has run yet
A blank cell is different: the row does not touch that rule. FIX-1481 holds ER-Devtool’s rows 4–6; rows 1–3 ride FIX-1320.
Two empty cells on the diagonal are the finding: each exit proof is its own rule in its own column, and two of the three are unowned. The third is held, not passed.
Kitchen-sink FIX-1455 no longer has a column — it left the set on Sep 20 (D9). ER-1, ER-2 and ER-3 were re-owned rather than left pointing at it; ER-3 was rewritten.
ER-15 was rewritten (this epic drives no child epic) and ER-19 retired, replaced by the three rules on the bottom row. FIX-1458 has had no column since it was canceled.
Nineteen further rules need no column and bind every row equally: 13 prohibitions (ER-5–14, 22, 24, 25), 4 run-the-set (ER-15–17, 23), 2 further proofs (ER-20, 21).
The set is open (ER-23) — a child filed against either remaining bottom-row cell takes that column and inherits every rule, as FIX-1481 did on Sep 20. A ticket is not a pass.
